headline: Law extends through 2028 the Bureau of Reclamation's authority to provide drought relief in western states and Hawaii.
what_it_does: This law renews a 1991 law called the Reclamation States Emergency Drought Relief Act, keeping it in effect through fiscal year 2028. That law lets the Bureau of Reclamation, a federal water agency, give drought help to Hawaii and certain western states. The summary does not describe any new programs or changes beyond extending the existing authority.

who_it_affects.group: Communities, farmers, and water users in western states and Hawaii
who_it_affects.how: They can continue to receive federal drought assistance from the Bureau of Reclamation through fiscal year 2028.
The agency keeps its legal authority to run drought relief programs for several more years.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; authority extended through fiscal year 2028.
